solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Local official's frenzied, hiding behind tree

indicators.note: hiding behind says the word for frenzied sits after the tree word

parts.note: the alder is a tree of damp ground
frenzied means wildly excited, manic

explanation.surface: A council worker has gone berserk and is lurking behind a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes what belongs to a council alderman, a senior local councillor.

clue.text: Vulgar look of the French after Revolution

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or behold

indicators.note: after Revolution says the French word is turned round

parts.note: du is French for of the

explanation.surface: A coarse look at the French after their Revolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Loud, of clothes or manners, means garish and tasteless.

clue.text: Not all feel destiny, like the one most likely to succeed?

definitions.text: like the one most likely to succeed

indicators.note: Not all says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people sense they are fated for great things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'succeed' here means inherit: the firstborn child is next in line.
explanation.definitionFit: The firstborn child is first in line to inherit, so most likely to take over.

clue.text: This person starting a row is more powerful

indicators.note: starting says the person word comes first

parts.note: this person, the setter, is me
a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: I begin an argument and prove the stronger party.
explanation.definitionFit: More substantial or forceful writing is called meatier.

clue.text: Architect's name written on wood

indicators.note: written on says the letter sits above the wood in this down light

parts.note: ash is a timber tree

explanation.surface: A designer's name is carved into a piece of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: John Nash was the Regency architect of Regent Street and Brighton Pavilion; the 's stands for is.

clue.text: Cold parrot suffering in shelter by house

indicators.note: suffering hints the letters of parrot are in a bad way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A chilly parrot is having a hard time in its shelter beside the house.
explanation.definitionFit: A roofed open shed beside a home protects a parked car.

clue.text: This manual is wrong about one man's economic theory

indicators.note: is wrong says the letters of the two words are mixed up

explanation.surface: This handbook misrepresents a particular economist's ideas.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Malthus argued population outgrows food; the adjective means relating to his theory.

clue.text: Prime thing for schoolkids to be put into schedule?

definitions.text: Prime thing for schoolkids to be put into schedule?

indicators.note: to be put into says the first letter goes inside the schedule word

parts.note: a timetable is a schedule

indicators.note: prime means first, so the opening letter of schoolkids is taken

explanation.surface: Something vital for pupils ought to be fitted into the school timetable.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: multiplication tables are a prime thing for children to learn.
explanation.definitionFit: Multiplication tables are a staple chanted by primary pupils, a core thing to learn.

clue.text: Levy a charge on one road vehicle

indicators.note: on says the numeral is placed after the levy word in this down-the-line charade

parts.note: to levy a charge is to impose a tax
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone imposes a fee on a single motorist.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is a hired car that carries passengers on the roads.

clue.text: Charity event offers enjoyment — a rider's fantastic

parts.note: fun is enjoyment

indicators.note: fantastic suggests wild invention, so the letters of a rider's are rearranged

parts.note: the word rider's, its S kept as a letter

explanation.surface: A charity gala is great fun, and one horseman in it is superb.
explanation.definitionFit: An event held to collect money for a good cause raises funds.

clue.text: Item of uniform placed on peg

parts.note: placed means put
a golf tee is a peg the ball sits on; on is just the joining word in the surface

explanation.surface: A piece of soldier's kit has been hung on a hook.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloth strip wound round the lower leg was part of military dress.

clue.text: Criticise neckwear and other garments

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
ties are worn round the neck

explanation.surface: A fashion critic slates the neckties and the rest of the outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Women's knickers are underwear, garments other than the neckwear just named.

clue.text: Bit of verse from writer not exciting (last bits of it are poor)

parts.note: a pen is a writing tool
tame means dull, not exciting

indicators.note: last bits of takes the final letter of each of the next three words

explanation.surface: A poet's lines are dull, and the endings are particularly feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: A line of five metrical feet is a unit of verse.

clue.text: Mister finally wears this thing possibly

definitions.text: Mister finally wears this thing possibly

indicators.note: wears says the last letter is held inside the rearranged pair
possibly says the letters of the two words could be put in another order
finally takes the last letter of Mister

explanation.surface: In the end a man puts this on for bed, perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signalled by 'possibly' gives NIGHTSHIT, and 'wears' puts the final R inside it; read whole, the clue also describes the bedtime garment a man puts on.
explanation.definitionFit: A long loose shirt is worn in bed by men, such as a mister.

clue.text: Faithful disciple person with time could become

indicators.note: could become says the letters of person and time are turned into something else

explanation.surface: A loyal follower of the faith might arise from someone given time.
explanation.definitionFit: Simon Peter was the apostle Jesus called the rock, a leading follower.

clue.text: Something made for attaching to tube

indicators.note: attaching to says the first word is joined on before the tube word

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
a duct is a tube or channel

explanation.surface: A fitting designed to be fixed onto a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods are what a factory turns out: anything manufactured is its output.

clue.text: See 14
Fix shrub that's been trimmed at the front

indicators.text: that's been trimmed at the front
indicators.note: trimmed at the front says the shrub word loses its opening letter

parts.note: privet is a hedging shrub

explanation.surface: A gardener secures a hedge plant whose front has been clipped.
explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something firmly is to rivet it, as with metal pins.

clue.text: Worries horses

definitions.meaning: worries as a verb: pesters or frets someone
old or poor horses are called ...

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: nagging is persistent pestering, and a nag is a feeble horse.

clue.text: Part of body that should be supple — no hesitation

indicators.note: no says the hesitation sound is removed from the supple word

parts.note: limber means supple, flexible
er is the sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A flexible body part should bend without any hesitating.
explanation.definitionFit: An arm or leg is a jointed member of the body.

clue.text: Active person drinking very little port

indicators.note: drinking says the doer takes the small letter inside

parts.note: a doer is someone who gets things done
v is the short form of very, little signalling the abbreviation

explanation.surface: A busy man sips only a drop of fortified wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink being sipped, but it is the definition: a harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Dover is the English Channel harbour town nearest France.

clue.text: Bad person with heavenly body hugged by the old man

indicators.note: hugged by says the celestial word is held inside the father word

parts.note: the old man is slang for father, dad
a star is a heavenly body

explanation.surface: A villain in possession of a celestial object, embraced by his father.
explanation.definitionFit: A dastard is an old word for a contemptible coward or scoundrel.

clue.text: Big cars will get walkers avoiding street

indicators.note: avoiding says the street letters are left out of the walkers word

parts.note: strollers are people out walking

explanation.surface: Large cars will pick up pedestrians who keep off the road.
explanation.walkthrough: Rollers is slang for Rolls-Royce cars.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolls-Royces are nicknamed Rollers, and they are large luxury cars.

clue.text: Sinatra seen to be exceptional craftsman

indicators.note: exceptional, read as out of the ordinary, tells us to rearrange the singer's name

explanation.surface: Frank Sinatra is acclaimed as an outstanding master of his craft.
explanation.definitionFit: A skilled manual worker who makes things by hand is a craftsman.

clue.text: Exciting quality of African party in capital city

indicators.note: in says the party goes inside the capital

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
the ANC is South Africa's African National Congress

explanation.surface: An African political party holds a thrilling rally in a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Romance is the glamour or thrilling appeal of adventure.

clue.text: An artist takes in shy cat

parts.note: a shy is a throw or attempt, a go
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: A painter adopts a timid cat.
explanation.definitionFit: The Angora is a long-haired breed of domestic cat from Turkey.

clue.text: Lover once passionate admitting end of her urge

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: admitting says the passionate word lets a letter in

parts.note: hot means passionate

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of her

explanation.surface: A former lover, still passionate, lets her desire show.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhort is to urge someone strongly, to press them on.

clue.text: See 26
Promiscuity costing nothing, nothing

parts.note: something free costs nothing
love means nil, nothing, in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: Casual sex comes at no cost whatsoever.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names sexual relations without commitment or marriage, i.e. promiscuity.

clue.text: It's beyond the directors to be honest

parts.note: above means higher than, beyond
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Something is beyond the company directors' grasp.
explanation.definitionFit: Open and legitimate dealings are said to be above board, done in plain sight.

clue.text: Lord beheaded king in play, then left

indicators.note: beheaded says the king's name loses its first letter

parts.note: King Lear is Shakespeare's tragedy

explanation.surface: A nobleman cut off a stage monarch's head, then departed.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer, one of the lords.

clue.text: One woman who may give others the sack?

definitions.text: One woman who may give others the sack?

parts.words: One woman who may give others the sack
parts.note: not a boss firing staff: a sack is a loose shift dress, so this woman sews them

explanation.definitionFit: A seamstress makes clothes, including the shapeless dress called a sack.
